correctness.rationale: For every 0<t<=1, any ℓ1^3 projection onto ker(1,1,t) is I-u(1,1,t), and positive weights b=t(1+t)/2 and 1 on the three fixed-sign column lower bounds give exact r=1+t/(1+t+t²). The explicit u=((1+t)/(2s),(1+t)/(2s),t/s) attains r and equality forces it uniquely. The isometric disjoint-support measure embedding and contractive Borel mass retraction give λ(W,M)=r. Kania–Lewicki Daugavet duality gives λ(Y,C)=1+r. Any weak-star continuous minimizing projection has a continuous coefficient map g(s)∈ker(1,1,t), ℓ1 norm <=r, whose first two interval averages are the unique saturated columns. The common boundary would force g=(0,0,-r), contradicting t>0. Monotonicity proves the exact full interval. The included pure-Python exact-rational verifier passed 9600 assertions, supplementing the analytical proof.

value.rationale: This establishes the full sharp fixed-codimension-two interval asked in Kania–Lewicki 2026 Question 6.2, including an exact, nonattained 7/3 endpoint compelled by the real planar Grünbaum bound. The spaces are natural mean-constraint subspaces of C[0,1], not arbitrary finite samples. The incompatible norming-face mechanism explains why a finite-dimensional best projection cannot be implemented by continuous dual coefficients. No higher-codimension or complex assertion is made.
